description: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals is a major pharmaceutical company that develops and sells drugs covering areas of immunology, oncology, ophthalmology, and rare diseases. During the COVID-19 outbreak it developed a widely used monoclonal antibody treatment. Other flagship products include Eylea, an injection to treat age-related macular degeneration and other eye conditions; Dupixent, a therapy for inflammatory diseases like atopic dermatitis, asthma, and chronic rhinosinusitis; and Libtayo, for certain types of cancer. The company was incorporated in 1988.

rankings.title: Change the World
rankings.itemDescription: Regeneron studies the root causes of diseases and identifies new therapies for rare and ultrarare conditions at its genetics center. For example, the company has been studying conditions such as fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP), a disabling disease that transforms muscles, ligaments, and other tissue into bone, and is conducting late-stage trials of a FOP treatment. Regeneron is also testing a novel approach to treating lipodystrophy, a rare disorder that leads to low levels of body fat and its abnormal distribution, plus reduced leptin levels, disrupting metabolism.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription: Regeneron’s anti-coronavirus cocktail REGEN-COV was provisionally approved in November 2020 to treat COVID-19 symptoms, and may also reduce its spread. But to develop the important therapy, the biotechnology and pharmaceuticals firm had to keep its own researchers and other staff safe as one of the first U.S. hotspots exploded just miles from its Tarrytown, N.Y., headquarters. The company sent nonessential workers home while implementing safety measures in its research labs. By spring of 2020 Regeneron was providing regular COVID testing for employees, and indefinite paid leave for those infected to recover and quarantine. The firm donated coronavirus-testing components to its home state, with hundreds of staff voluntarily working overtime and weekends to produce them. Regeneron also rolled out a new five-year responsibility strategy organized around stakeholders, including new diversity and inclusion measures after the summer’s wave of protests against anti-Black police brutality. Says one employee: “As an African American male, it’s nice to know that I work for a company that really puts its money where its mouth is regarding making changes in underserved communities.”

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription: The biotechnology company produces medicines and treatments for allergic and inflammatory diseases, eye diseases, cancers, and more. Regeneron became a household name in 2020 when the U.S. government granted it a $450 million federal contract to develop an antibody drug to treat COVID-19. Former U.S. President Donald Trump reportedly received the treatment while hospitalized with the illness in October 2020.

Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription: The biopharmaceutical company develops and manufactures medicines designed to treat a range of illnesses, including asthma, chronic pain, cancer, and infectious diseases. In the latter category, Regeneron is deeply involved in the pursuit of treatments for COVID-19.

rankings.title: Change the World
rankings.itemDescription: The world has battled Ebola since 1976, but only late last year did it get therapies that should meaningfully reduce the virus’s death toll. In a randomized clinical trial conducted during an outbreak in Africa, one such drug—Regeneron’s antibody cocktail, EB3—proved so clearly effective in reducing mortality that the trial was ended early. Regeneron is now racing to develop a comparable cocktail for COVID-19.
